findings.reason: a node implementing the bound as written would silently blank real coordinators, and the queue waits that produce this are the weeks-long queue waits admission itself creates, so the defect grows with the behaviour §11 exists to serve.
findings.text: §11 asserts "The answer for every plan inside the window does not change", but a run id is minted when the dispatch request is queued while `dispatched_at` is written when admission launches it, so a document can be named months-old and still hold a row the resolver keeps; measured on reckon's committed ledger at 2026-11-06T11:40Z (6,912 per-run documents, 168 h window, the section's own one-day margin), the bound reads 372 documents instead of 6,912 and turns three plans from a named coordinator to unowned: `a-finished-plan-closes` (base `efd0ee8c-9d4e-4fa3-a440-ac05791d4758`, dispatched 2026-11-05T21:23Z, run id stamped 2026-10-27), `the-mcp-answers-the-question-asked` (dispatched 2026-11-05T20:14Z) and `the-suite-is-green-at-head` (dispatched 2026-11-02T22:04Z), with the fleet's own long-queued §3–§7 nodes of this plan among the 14 skipped-but-kept rows

findings.reason: the fixture as specified cannot fail on the defect the section ships, so a node would deliver a green gate and a wrong resolver; the fixture needs one long-queued document whose run-id stamp predates the bound and whose dispatch instant is inside the window.
findings.text: §11's done-when asserts "the resolved coordinators equal those the base returns" on a fixture holding only documents wholly older than the window and documents inside it, which contains no document whose name predates the bound while its `dispatched_at` falls inside the window, so the assertion passes on exactly the code that fails on real rows
